reviews.review: Live, Laugh, LORT.
very good!
i love lort (and the game)

Booted it up thinking, “Haha, funny name, this’ll be trash.”
Game: “Surprise, idiot.”
Now I’m 20 hours in, dehydrated, and emotionally invested in pixels with better character development than most Netflix shows.

LORT plays like someone merged peak childhood fantasy, unmedicated ADHD, and a Reddit thread at 3 AM, then somehow made it good.
Combat is so smooth I started dodging IRL responsibilities on instinct.
The soundtrack goes unnecessarily hard for a game that sounds like a typo.

The dialogs have the exact energy of “I lived, b*tch,” and every boss feels like a personal attack for choices I made in 2013.
I keep saying “one more quest” like it’s not the biggest lie since “I’ll just check my phone real quick.”

Pros:

Accidentally fun.

Accidentally deep.

Accidentally my new personality.

Cons:

I don’t live in this world, which feels like a design flaw.

My friends keep asking where I’ve been. I tell them I’m “out of office (in LORT).”

Installed LORT as a meme.
Stayed because it’s the only thing in my life that’s not disappointing me.

10/10, would LORT again.

The flow state of this game feels really good especially compared to how it felt in previous demos/playtests. 

The good: Weapon damage/enemy health feels good. They used to feel very damage/bullet sponge-y for the volume of enemies, and I think the balance to make them less sponge-y feels good. It also makes it feel good when you get a combo going that works for your damage type. Movement speed is definitely faster than prior builds and I'm glad they've moved in the direction of being able to move faster in general.

The bad: I think unrecoverable grey health is not a very fun mechanic, at least outside of something like a hard mode, or some kind of way to restore it. If you die more than 2-3 times, enemies in areas 3 and beyond will likely JUST one shot you and I don't really understand why. I also don't think your items dropping on death is a particularly exciting mechanic either. 

I'm looking forward to what the devs support this game with over time, I think the comments of solo being "too" hard are a bit far fetched, it's definitely harder but I don't think it's THAT difficult, maybe they could tune solo a little different but it's not as bad as some people are saying

If you're looking for a like 3 hour game sure it's good but none of the classes are balanced well in solo. Astrid is the only good class because turns out leech with infinite mob cleave and stun on demand is a lot better than puddle of piss and "I'm gonna knock every mob up and away from me". 

Map design is also kind of weird with the time design. If you get good with abusing the physics of bunny hopping after air dodging you can get around fast. Otherwise, you're often not able to explore the map well cause 3rd day comes fast.

LORT has the potential to be a really great roguelike, but right now the difficulty scaling is absurd. the movement speed, lack of healing, and lack of items that feel like they actually add stats is just awful. it's incredibly difficult to get better weapons and the day/night cycle scaling is too much. 

I think with a few changes (such as movement and difficulty scaling) the game has so much potential, but for right now I'll be shelfing this until more updates come out.

I really enjoyed playing the full version today. A few things stood out to me in particular.

The difficulty curve feels very well balanced and gradually increasing. As someone who has spent most of his life playing FPS shooters, this was a refreshing change. You actually have to focus and put in effort to progress, which makes every encounter feel meaningful. The enemies are interesting, and every match feels like a real challenge. This is an excellent game for “gamer dads” who don’t have the time to endlessly grind but still want a rewarding experience.

One thing that felt a bit confusing was the party system. If someone needs to leave, there isn’t a clear or intuitive way to transfer the host role to another player. That could definitely be improved.

Overall though, hats off to the developers. I really hope there’s a lot more content coming, because this game has strong potential and feels like it’s heading in the right direction. I genuinely enjoyed it.

The graphics are solid, the game feels polished, movement is natural, and nothing feels clunky or unfinished.

The only bug I noticed was during camp clearing. If you pick up two or three totems around the camp, the camp can get stuck and doesn’t give loot, because the game still indicates that enemies are nearby even when there aren’t any.

The core gameplay is fun, a lot of the complaints about difficulty and weapon variety are the type of things that can be adjusted and improved as part of the early access process. But there's the shell of a fun game loop here that's worth the price of admission imo

So some quick thoughts... the core loop works, especially with friends: fight, loot, stack power-ups, revive each other, repeat. When a run comes together and your build starts popping off, it feels great.

The early game can be a bit unforgiving until you really understand how things are supposed to work. Without a couple of key starting items, some runs feel rough right out of the gate. Loadout tweaks could help a lot here, like letting players start with a specific weapon or a few common items so builds come online faster.

The mechanics themselves are solid, but the UI gets messy once buffs start stacking, and some levels could use better tuning. More quest variety and deeper skill trees would also add a lot to long-term replayability.

I get that this is early access, and overall the game actually feels fairly mature already. I just hope “early access” doesn’t become a crutch for slow-rolling changes, because there’s a genuinely good idea here. It’s worth jumping in even at this stage, and I’m excited to see how it evolves if the devs keep iterating with intention.

tl;dr watch a youtube to learn core mechanics till ingame UI / QoL / feedback come online and enjoy, 5/7 with rice.

[The following review is Early Access + Solo Player. Ain't sponsoring this for friends since it's not fun alone...]

The short: As it is? This game sucks. I say this as someone with quite a bit of time in Risk of Rain 2 (direct comparison made on X for the game), and seeking something titled "The Next RoR2". Every game claiming to be that, has sucked (Endless Alice, Mycopunk), and this continues the trend. This game DEFINITELY needs time to cook if it's going to be anything good.

The long:

LORT is a multiplayer-focused roguelite with a few different characters and most importantly, brutal difficulty for all the wrong reasons. The game loop is supposedly simple. Pick a character, drop into the hub, take a quest/mission target, go into the field, DO THE JOB, AND GET OUT OF THERE.

+Game demands leveling up and getting strong. This is an obvious starting point to beating enemies and the boss ahead.
+Game informs (too frequently) about the color/stat system. Characters have color coordinated stats for obvious ease of power increase. Red for STR (Melee), green for AGI (Ranged), and blue for INT (Magical).
+Game has loot. Duh, it's a "Risk of Rain 2" ripoff. Unfortunately...

-Game unfortunately leaves stat upgrades to random chance. You'll need to go to enemy camps with your color above it, clear the enemies out, and gain your color reward. If you're unlucky and don't see your color, you're getting paltry upgrades versus your fat 25% damage/skill boost per upgrade for matching color.
--Enemies at the start are wildly tanky, and while this is to be expected later on, at the start? The game is not kind. You'll be kiting or dying in melee very very fast to an enemy swarm if you aren't paying attention. 
---Even with the scaling, you seem to just...don't do damage. It's never enough to breathe easy and go "Hey I can clear the trash and focus on threats!" like...every other game in the roaming enemy killing genre akin to Risk of Rain. This is a major issue, since EVERYTHING YOU DO involves swarms of enemies or tanky foes that need to be concentrated on.
----Bosses in particular, if the first quest is to be iterated upon after, are extremely boring. They spam area of effect attacks, they summon more additional minions, and to top it off, they take 8-20 minutes to kill if you weren't lucky enough to get scaling. I hear a horror story of the final boss, but I don't think I'll ever see it. 
-----Game also has useless loot! I shouldn't have the misfortune of seeing the meme oontz oontz oontz clap soundpad THIS OFTEN. It's a useless drop, and while funny - not exactly conclusive to a winning run unless there's HIDDEN DEPTHS TO IT, which nobody's talking about. Bad bonus: loot is wildly expensive to acquire while gold is slowly gained. I feel oppressed and helpless, versus 'starting out and getting stronger' in this game. Always too poor to open treasure chests in a reasonable time frame.

<Crossbows also suck so bad. You use it for the right click, then go back to ANY OTHER WEAPON due to doing 40 damage and having to reload. Regular bow hits harder, hits more often, and the pierce shot actually is an okay horde-attack move...in a game about hitting groups of enemies.>

Any true multiplayer gripes or greatness I can't account for, since I'm the only one in my circle that has this. Arc Raiders eats most of their time - good for them.

The game needs more. More options for playability like difficulty settings/scaling settings (Endless Alice blows wang but you can custom tailor that game to your EVERY NEED. ANYONE can play it and unlock content before going to harder/intended difficulty). More weapons because the equipment variety isn't great (neither's the damage). More options in terms of playable characters. More common sense - chests should start low and scale. 30 gold is a steep ask for garbage, let alone actual good chests. Weapon chests shouldn't give random loot, it should give color/class specific random loot. Nothing like a magic sword with zero scaling out the box after 5 runs with no keys in the first zone!

It's rough. The game has great 'look at this!' kind of feel and it sounds great, but when you settle down and play it, it's full of problems. People who jerk off with sharp cheese graters and sleep on hot spiked coal will love it, but...I play Roguelites because time's limited. No endorphins here. Everyone wants to make the ballbuster difficulty game from the start, instead of leading up to it. LET'S PLAY THE GAME:

[Is it better than the game it's drawing direct comparison from by self-admission: Risk of Rain 2?]: NOT EVEN CLOSE

[Is it better than personal Indie GOTYAY: Gravity Circuit?]: It's different. Inferior by grounds of being multiplayer focused ANYWAY.

[Is it better than personal Multiplayer Indie Roguelite of choice Gunfire Reborn?]HELL NO.

This game needs time to become something great...hope it does. Otherwise I've gotta adopt the 'no new games' policy. Too many pitfalls for cash.

LORT combines some of the best things about megabonk and Risk of Rain 2. As someone who’s newer to this genre and style of game I will say that the difficulty is spot on for what this game is. As soon as you realize the attributes and their importance, while also using weapons that scale with your attribute, you’re going to trivialize most boss fights whether playing solo or with a group. 

Me and a buddy had one game where he had about 10 bricks on him and chucked them all at the first boss and all we had to do was tap her and she was dead. Whole fight lasted like 30 seconds max. 

Point is, difficulty is perfect for where we’re at with the game and the items. I do think that the gold prices can be adjusted for multiplayer play a little more, at least with 2 players the scaling of the chests gets kind of overwhelming toward the end.

This game is tough—and that’s what makes it great.
Running in with just one friend, we get absolutely challenged, but that’s exactly the kind of experience we’re here for. It feels rewarding when you survive and brutal when you don’t.

I’d love to see more characters added and eventually a way to upgrade or swap starting weapons, but even as-is, the game is a blast.

If you’re even slightly on the fence, just give it a shot. It’s good fun, and hopping into their Discord to find a group or just hang out with other players makes it even better.

LORT is a fun game, don't get me wrong. I've played it Singleplayer Only since neither I don't have friends to play with, and there's not Open Lobbies. My best run was getting to the Mountain Peak and getting halfway through the boss before dying (which I think this run took me about an hour roughly) and I know they're going to tweak Singleplayer since I think there's no balance change between Single and Multiplayer. There is slight replay-ability with the upgrading system (e.g. getting more health potions, spawning in with more gold) and each run does feel slightly different.

It's also an Early Access game, which means it's pretty barebones. There's only two quests where you steal food items and then escape, expect in the trailer, its shown that you put these food items in the cauldron (which you don't in game). Some enemies do need a bit of balancing (e.g. the goblins who trot around and throw molotovs are a pain in the penny to kill over being a challenge). That being said, they are working on the game as we speak and this is made by the developers who worked on Early Fortnite Seasons (which to my guess also means they worked on Save the World, which if so, is a big W)

For £8.44 (Introductory Sale) or £12.79 (Base Price as of writing), I don't think its a bad price for both parties. Not too expensive for the gamers, neither too cheap for developers to make money. I think if it was £15 or more, that would be taking the piss.

So that's why I feel this is more a Mixed Review over a Positive one, spite speaking highly of the game.
Would I recommend getting the game? Yeah, its good to play with friends if you've got some
Would I recommend getting the game to support the developers? For the Introductory Offer, yeah, I wouldn't argue.
Would I recommend getting the game and expecting 20+ hours out of this game? Ehhh, probably not for the moment but that'll change when the stuff from the road map gets added
